actions: Start flood irrigation today, delivering 30 mm of water per application; repeat every 7‑10 days until the flowering stage (≈ day 60).
Apply a 5‑cm layer of straw mulch or plastic mulch immediately after irrigation to conserve soil moisture and lower surface temperature.
Incorporate 10 t ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or organic manure into the top 15 cm of soil within the next 3 days to raise organic carbon levels.
Monitor soil moisture daily with a tensiometer; maintain field capacity (~0.32 m³ m⁻³) and avoid waterlogging.
Conduct a visual field walk every 2 days for wilting, pest (aphids, bollworms) and disease (Fusarium/Verticillium wilt) symptoms.
Request a rapid‑refresh NDVI/NDWI satellite pass (or use a drone) in 7 days to verify vegetation recovery.

steps.finding: Implement immediate flood irrigation combined with soil organic matter amendment to alleviate critical water stress and improve soil health.
actions: Start flood irrigation today, delivering 30 mm of water per application; repeat every 7‑10 days until the flowering stage (≈ day 60).
Apply a 5‑cm layer of straw mulch or plastic mulch immediately after irrigation to conserve soil moisture and lower surface temperature.
Incorporate 10 t ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or organic manure into the top 15 cm of soil within the next 3 days to raise organic carbon levels.
Monitor soil moisture daily with a tensiometer; maintain field capacity (~0.32 m³ m⁻³) and avoid waterlogging.
Conduct a visual field walk every 2 days for wilting, pest (aphids, bollworms) and disease (Fusarium/Verticillium wilt) symptoms.
Request a rapid‑refresh NDVI/NDWI satellite pass (or use a drone) in 7 days to verify vegetation recovery.
steps.justification: Satellite imagery shows severe vegetation stress (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) caused by a lack of rainfall. Soil health is otherwise excellent (pH optimal, high nitrogen, suitable texture) but organic carbon is low, limiting moisture retention. Prompt irrigation will restore plant water status, while adding compost will boost organic carbon, reduce evaporation, and prevent future stress. Market prices are strong, so rescuing the crop now maximizes profitability.
